network create internal IPv4-only sentinel bridge
create responder (pinned Python only; fixed 127.0.0.1:45173 -> 18080/tcp request; private socket directory only)
create TCP sentinel (no publish or mounts)
exec responder: one loopback HTTP GET after private listener socket appears
exec sentinel: one loopback TCP positive control
exec responder: inspect routes and one cross-bridge TCP attempt against owned sentinel
http_sequence: Inside responder GET 127.0.0.1:18080/fictional-health; require exact fictional body
Ubuntu GET 127.0.0.1:45173/fictional-health only if exact effective binding; skip when Docker explicitly reports target empty/null
Ubuntu GET /fictional-health over private Unix socket; no published port used
evidence: fsynced pre-send journal and returned inspection/probe receipts
result with counts, unexpected failures, captured/uncertain resources, preservation hashes and journal SHA-256

preflight SHA-256 and byte count bound to the immutable claim and exact execution journal prefix

preclaim.exclusive: Both claim and audit paths must be absent. Reserve the audit directory with mkdir; retain even on failure and refuse reuse.
preclaim.counting: The three actions are the first three of the existing 14 normal Docker actions. No separate or duplicate metadata commands.
preclaim.transition: Journal exactly one pre-send and one successful receipt for each of the three checks, in order. Verify source and locally observed endpoint identity, seal the audit, and exclusively reserve the claim. Adopt the exact verified audit prefix before dispatching mutations.

operational_transport.scope: Fictional diagnostic on an owner-controlled Docker Desktop WSL2 host; no immutable daemon continuity or cryptographic attestation.
operational_transport.config: New empty mode-0700 configuration directory in the exclusive preflight audit. Reject Docker/TLS/API overrides.
operational_transport.routing: The first CLI call inspects the default context; all remaining calls use the fixed Unix host explicitly. Recheck the CLI and socket filesystem identities. No extra negotiation command or Engine API call from the runner.
operational_transport.uncertainty: Loss, timeout, identity drift or uncertain mutation stops all Docker dispatch, including cleanup. Retain all known remaining IDs and any ambiguous operation; separate owner inspection required.
operational_transport.ordinary_failure: Only a healthy fixed target with trusted create receipts or inspected ownership may receive the existing bounded exact-ID cleanup.
operational_transport.accounting: The ceiling counts CLI invocations, not the Engine API messages the approved Docker CLI necessarily sends as part of those invocations.
operational_transport.limitation: A silent upstream daemon substitution at an unchanged socket with indistinguishable responses cannot be detected. A matching Engine ID at preflight is a point-in-time observation.
